description: Draft contracts this build can read ONLY through the explicitly requested rule-V7 lane. These are not released contracts: neither type has a row in the shared schemas/versions.json, a published schemaVersion of its own, a w3id URL or a release tag, and nothing in this file changes that. Each entry pins the exact bytes of one draft file by the commit of the development repository that owns the type and the SHA-256 of those bytes, which is how docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md V7 requires a draft to be read: selection runs against the pinned bytes, never against a repository's main at run time. Two revisions are pinned per type and they are different things: `commit` is the revision of the contract bytes this library compiles and validates against, and `suiteCommit` is the revision of the owning repository's development conformance suite whose manifest `scripts/capability/draft-vectors.mjs` executes. They are separate keys because the two files move at different times, and because the suite carries the rule labels this file quotes: a claim about C1/C2/C3 is a claim about the suite revision, never about the contract revision. Where they are equal, `suiteCommit` repeats `commit` so the check is uniform. `src/drafts.js` re-verifies every digest the first time a draft is loaded and refuses to read on a mismatch. The lane is never the default: with no explicit user decision these files are not read at all and a draft citation is 'any other value' under V5, exactly as it was before the lane existed. This registry is deliberately separate from schemas/provenance.json, which lists released contracts only and stays that way.
rule: docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md rule V7 (FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#221/#226, text published at tag v0.6.0)

scheduledPublication.note: A scheduled future release is a decision about that type, not a licence to publish it here. Until the release lands these entries stay drafts: no schemaVersion claim, no fixed alias, no registry row, no support claim.

retrieved: 2026-11-14 (contract bytes), re-measured 2026-11-16T04:20Z for this re-pin: all five pinned targets were fetched again from the owning repositories' default branch and hashed, and the two contract files came back byte-identical
retrievalMethod: Every digest recorded here was computed from bytes actually downloaded, never from a HEAD content-length and never from raw.githubusercontent.com at a moving branch name: the GitHub contents API was asked for each path at `ref=main`, the base64 body was decoded to a file, that file was re-read and hashed, and the API's git blob sha was compared with the blob sha recomputed from the bytes on disk (all five matched, which is what proves each download is whole). Each manifest was additionally read out of a local Git object database at the same commit (`git show <commit>:<path>`) and `cmp`-ed against the API bytes. The raw-main URLs in `citation` are what a reader cites and what the advisory freshness check probes; they are not how these numbers were measured, because that CDN was seen to serve pre-merge bytes for minutes after a merge on 2026-11-16.

FHT.suiteCommitNote: The suite moved on 2026-11-16 (FHT-Specification#47 promoted four real-data pilot cases and #46 added rule-accountability and gzip cases); the contract did not. `fht.json` is byte-identical at `226f923c` and at this revision - the same git blob `89b7dea728efcbd5d46f95c3ec0e87b63a40623e` at both, checked with `git rev-parse <commit>:fht.json` - so this re-pin moves no contract byte and the contract pin stays where it is on purpose: it names the revision the library's compiled bytes come from, not the newest commit in the repository. That distinction earned its keep within minutes: FHT-Specification's main advanced to 09dafdf8182c84c3689bd5efeeafcdb7a803a443 (#48, an AGENTS.md guidance port) after this measurement, and `git rev-parse` shows both `fht.json` (blob 89b7dea7...) and `conformance/manifest.json` (blob a7f2dca5...) unchanged at that commit, which the contents API confirmed at ref=main (9fd8c0b2a4638d5d..., 65615 bytes) - so the pin stays at the revision it was measured at, and neither a moved head nor an unchanged digest is a reason to rewrite a commit field. A future re-pin moves this value only when the bytes move.
FHT.verification: Read from the FHT-Specification checkout with `git show <commit>:fht.json`; the same bytes are present at that repository's main head be9bcc825f55db92852fd882ffba4c1c214f53db (checked 2026-11-16T04:20Z, digest identical) and are fetched byte-equal over HTTPS from the pinned commit URL (200, 29430 bytes, sha256 59ad9641...). These are the re-pinned bytes: the released fair-bioheaders 0.11.0 wheel still bundles the previous draft (sha256 11c69d66...), so a differential against the installed toolkit compares against older draft bytes and is labelled accordingly. The suite is pinned apart from the contract: `conformance/manifest.json` at suiteCommit be9bcc825f55db92852fd882ffba4c1c214f53db was fetched from the contents API at `ref=main` (200, 65615 bytes on disk, sha256 9fd8c0b2a4638d5ddc0bf9b5d1e96c66778b26bcf8f93975aafb707d8f2b702c, git blob a7f2dca5cbcaf6ef034e357c9683a5432ee9ca8e recomputed from the downloaded bytes and equal to the value the API states) and `cmp`-ed byte-equal against `git show be9bcc82:conformance/manifest.json` from a local object database; it declares 72 vectors whose contract rule labels are C1, C2 and C3. The previous pin described 56250 bytes at 9b07179497bdc7247d6ead2404d9d5fdee48308a58b385bd4cd9a7e91450053a from `24d3b033`, a 66-vector suite; the diff is six added vectors and none removed - `fht-fasta-gzip-multimember` and `fht-fasta-gzip-sequence-tampered`, plus four parent-link cases (`fht-fasta-parent-subset-citing-whole`, `fht-fasta-parent-masked-exact`, `fht-fasta-parent-real-digest-wrong-file`, `fht-fasta-parent-case-folded-digest`) that the suite itself marks `promotion: candidate-unreviewed`, i.e. derived from the pilot evidence in FHT-Specification#45 and not yet reviewed by a second reader. Four of this suite's 72 vectors therefore carry an unreviewed expectation, and a pass on them is draft-lane evidence about this build's behaviour, never a claim that the expectation is right. A second re-pin pass is expected: the owning repository's examples-and-vectors tracker, FHT-Specification#8, is still open and every one of its seven checklist boxes read unchecked (`- [ ]`) when it was fetched at 2026-11-16T04:40Z, so this suite will move again - and when it does the digest is re-measured first and the count re-read from those same bytes, never the reverse.
FHT.note: An FHT header is a FASTA `;~` block like FHR, so it shares the FASTA container; the type is decided by the record's own `schema` citation. Its conformance rules are C1 (contract validation), C2 (schema-URL closure) and C3 (parent-link verification) - text in the FHT-Specification conformance README. C2 is inside the pinned bytes; C3 is implemented here in src/parent-links.js.

FHGM.suiteCommitNote: The FHGM suite pin is stated for the first time by this re-pin; before it, `drafts/provenance.json` carried no suite revision for FHGM and the draft-lane run could only label itself UNPINNED. It is not equal to `commit`, and the two revisions are not interchangeable claims: `commit` `ac3d37b3` is where this build's record-contract bytes come from and is not moved by anything here, while the suite has since taken FHGM-Specification#16/#17/#18/#19. The suite is pinned at the owning repository's main head as measured at 2026-11-16T04:24Z, which is one commit ahead of PR #19's merge commit `57118c52` (`c503ecf3` is an AGENTS.md guidance port touching no target file); `git rev-parse` shows the manifest, the record contract and the overlay are the **same git blobs** at `57118c52` and at `c503ecf3` - manifest `40c81f03942baefbd3a7419a05d79bfd46a06f57`, contract `1fb066b8da5bf5bb462462763b0676dfb7d3d2ff`, overlay `f6835cfa470b979687c6475c88cb59ddf5f30c1a` - so the digest pin names the bytes exactly at both revisions and the newer commit is chosen only so the advisory freshness check compares like with like.
FHGM.verification: Read from the FHGM-Specification checkout with `git show <commit>:development/model/fhgm-model.schema.json`; the same bytes are present at that repository's main head (checked 2026-11-16T04:24Z, digest identical to `ac3d37b3` and to `c503ecf3`: git blob 1fb066b8da5bf5bb462462763b0676dfb7d3d2ff, 9564 bytes, sha256 bf1553ca...) and are fetched byte-equal over HTTPS from the pinned commit URL (200, 9564 bytes, sha256 bf1553ca...). FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification pins the same bytes for its CEDAR draft snapshot at templates/cedar/drafts/provenance.json (sha256 bf1553ca..., re-pinned by #237/#238), so this consumer and the publication authority agree on what the draft is. The suite manifest was fetched from the contents API at `ref=main` (200, 51114 bytes on disk, sha256 0d2790151c4a29551e9b92fb6b3c3c62ea062f2889ffbd00b3c425e7b6da3458, git blob 40c81f03942baefbd3a7419a05d79bfd46a06f57 recomputed from the downloaded bytes and equal to the value the API states) and `cmp`-ed byte-equal against `git show c503ecf3:development/conformance/manifest.json` from a local object database; it declares 43 vectors labelled B1 and K1-K6, all of them `fhgff3` files that carry the records in `x-fhgm-models`. The previous count this repository could state at all was 31: the diff is twelve added `dmel-*` vectors and none removed (census 31 sealed to 43: 14 valid, 29 invalid), promoted by FHGM-Specification#18 from the real-data *Drosophila melanogaster* chr4 fixtures - its promotion packet counts them as the ten gap-proof rejections plus the two positive anchors the promoted pointer cases require - under an explicit `Status: DRAFT`, 'the expectations recorded in manifest.json for the 12 dmel-* vectors require independent review'. A pass by this build on those twelve is therefore evidence about what this reader does with them, never a review of whether the expectation is right. Three of the twelve are labelled K4 (`dmel-snapshot-v1`, `dmel-target-absent`, `dmel-target-transcript-row`); all three reached a real K4 verdict against the file's own feature rows, so none was scored by assumption.

transportOverlay.note: Transport-only overlay. It no longer pins one FHGFF3 file identity: FHGM-Specification#17 (maintainer dual-base decision of 2026-11-15) rewrote it as a closed `anyOf` of two branch pairings - the v0.5.0 citation set with `schemaVersion` '1.1', or the v0.6.0 citation set with '1.2' - so a citation and a stated version that contradict each other are rejected and neither pairing falls back to the other. FHGFF3 1.0 stays inadmissible because R15 admits extension fields only from 1.1. It says nothing about record contents: those are the model contract above. It still requires a non-empty `x-fhgm-models` array of objects. This changes a documented divergence rather than recording a new number: `docs/CAPABILITY.md` used to answer 'does the overlay admit a current FHGFF3 header?' with 'no - a 1.2 carrier fails the overlay while satisfying R15', and the re-pinned bytes answer that question 'yes', which is why `src/fhgm.js`'s `overlay: true` is now the same width as the R15 reading on both released bases and the K1 test asserts the contradiction case instead. src/fhgm.js needs no change: it validates the header against whatever the pinned overlay says.

FHGM.note: FHGM is not a file header type: an FHGM record carries no `schema`, no `schemaVersion` and no `checksum`. Records ride inside an FHGFF3 header under the R15 extension key `x-fhgm-models`, the file keeps its released FHGFF3 citation and is routed by V1 to V3, and the file checksum covers every record byte (R3). The V7 lane therefore selects only the contract applied to the records. Model-level rules K1-K6 and the boundary B1 are drafted in FHGM-Specification; src/fhgm.js implements B1 and K1-K6, including K4 feature-target resolution against a feature layer - by default the enclosing file's own rows indexed for `type` and `ID` by src/features.js, or a resolver the caller injects - while full GFF3 feature validation remains with gff3-validator. A reading without a usable layer reports K4 `not-checked` or `unchecked`, never a pass and never a rejection. This sentence describes the consumer's implementation state and is not part of the pinned upstream bytes.
